etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Spanish patata, itself borrowed from Taíno batata (“sweet potato”).

definitions.definition: Solanum tuberosum or its edible starchy tuber.

quote.citation: 1891, “Condensed Replies to Various Letters”, in Leroy M[ilton] Yale, editor, Babyhood: The Mother’s Nursery Guide, Devoted to the Care of Children, volume VII, New York, N.Y., London: Babyhood Publishing Company, page 230, column 2:
quote.text: Do not let your child have potato for another year; he will probably take milk well enough after he is weaned.

quote.citation: 1912, C[harles] F[ord] Langworthy, Caroline L[ouisa] Hunt, Cheese and Its Economical Uses in the Diet (Farmers’ Bulletin 487), Washington, D.C.: Government Printing Office, page 24:
quote.text: The protein value of this dish is equal to that of 1⅛ pounds of potato and beef, the fuel value, however, being much in excess of these.

quote.citation: 1915, Annual Report of the Local Government Board for Scotland, page 17:
quote.text: A number of the children said that they had potato for breakfast, potato and herring for dinner, potato and milk for supper.

quote.citation: 2017, Anthony J. McMichael, Alistair Woodward, Cameron Muir, Climate Change and the Health of Nations, →ISBN, page 213:
quote.text: Potatoes were introduced to Ireland in 1590 after being brought to Europe by Spanish conquistadores from their place of origin in the South American Andes.

quote.citation: 2021 December 1, Nigel Harris, “St Pancras and King's Cross: 1947”, in RAIL, number 945, page 42:
quote.text: The rocketing popularity of potatoes in London's diet led to the conversion of the temporary GNR passenger station north of the canal [...] as a dedicated potato terminal, whose significant traffic was stolen from coastal shipping.

definitions.definition: (informal, UK) A conspicuous hole in a sock or stocking.
(humorous) A camera that takes poor-quality pictures.
(humorous, slang, computing) An underpowered computer or other device, especially when small in size.

quote.citation: 2017 March 17, Steven Messner, “Overwatch community donates PC parts to fan who could barely run it at 800x600”, in PC Gamer‎[1]:
quote.text: When most people refer to their computers as a potato they're being hyperbolic, but not Ethan. He plays Overwatch at 800x600 resolution with all settings on low and is excited when he gets 30 fps.

quote.citation: 2019 September 22, Benjamin Burns, “Meet the people making music with Mega Drives, Game Boys and gAtaris”, in Eurogamer‎[2]:
quote.text: If you want to have a go right now, then Famitracker will let you compose songs for the NES and it'll run on a Windows-operated potato.

definitions.definition: Metaphor for a person or thing of little value.

quote.citation: 1757, [Tobias George Smollett], The Reprisal: Or, The Tars of Old England. […], London:  […]  R[oberts] Baldwin, […], →OCLC, Act I, scene ii:
quote.text: I don't value Monſieur de Champignon a rotten potatoe;  […]

definitions.definition: (slang, transitive) To hit very hard; to pummel.

quote.citation: 2014, James Dixon, Arnold Furious, Bob Dahlstrom, The Raw Files: 1998, page 26:
quote.text: Bradshaw doesn't find much humour in it though, and beats the tar out of Dustin, potatoing him with every blow.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To hit with a thrown or fired potato.

quote.citation: 2017, A. J. Low, Sherlock Sam’s Orange Shorts: Special Edition:
quote.text: Yvonne and Lee Swee potatoed Deputy Lestrade multiple times before Sheriff Moran potatoed them both.  […]  Suddenly, Sheriff Moran heard the click click of an empty weapon. He turned to see that both Mayor Eliza and Kat had run out of ammunition.

definitions.definition: (onomatopoeia, often repeated) The rhythmic sound produced by a V-twin engine—a distinctive deep, throaty exhaust note.
